sections.sectionText: Title: Arts based teaching and learning in K-12 education. Description: In a rapidly changing educational landscape, teachers are increasingly seeking ways to engage learners, foster creativity, and support deeper understanding across disciplines. This course explores arts-based approaches to teaching and learning, examining how practices drawn from the visual, performing, literary, and digital arts can enrich educational experiences in diverse settings. We will explore research and theory on arts-based learning, creativity, embodiment, storytelling, reflection, and meaning-making, while considering the role of the arts in supporting equity, engagement, and student agency. This course draws on scholarship from arts-based education researchers as well as examples from classroom practice and community-based learning environments. Particular attention is given to a wide range of artistic practices, including painting, photography, fashion, music, theater, dance, poetry, storytelling, comics, podcasting, gaming, and other creative forms of expression. We will examine how these practices can support inquiry, communication, collaboration, and sense-making across educational contexts.

sections.sectionText: Storying as Qualitative Methodology offers a scholarly examination of storied frameworks (including storywork, counterstory, and social fiction) and provides students with a comprehensive understanding of various theoretical underpinnings inherent in storied research. Engaging with interdisciplinary perspectives, students will navigate diverse narrative landscapes, from personal narratives to speculative stories to cultural myths. Through rigorous analysis and interpretation, students will cultivate proficiency in discerning contextual nuances and thematic intricacies within narratives. Moreover, this course underscores the imperative of reflexivity and ethical considerations inherent in narrative research practices. By scrutinizing the manifold roles of storytelling in identity formation, meaning construction, and narrative disruption, students will gain profound insights into the multifaceted nature of qualitative inquiry. By integrating hands-on exercises, participants will hone their storytelling skills, whether through oral histories, digital narratives, or autoethnographic accounts.
